data.title: Results: Solaris Energy Infrastructure, Inc. Exceeded Expectations And The Consensus Has Updated Its Estimates
data.description:
Solaris Energy Infrastructure, Inc. (NYSE:SEI) just released its latest quarterly results and things are looking bullish. Statutory revenue of US$341m and earnings of US$0.42 both blasted past expectations, beating expectations by 25% and 51%, respectively, ahead of expectations. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. We thought readers would find it interesting to see the analysts latest (statutory) post-earnings forecasts for next year.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Taking into account the latest results, the most recent consensus for Solaris Energy Infrastructure from ten analysts is for revenues of US$1.87b in 2027. If met, it would imply a huge 100% increase on its revenue over the past 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to bounce 349% to US$4.96. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of US$1.87b and earnings per share (EPS) of US$4.40 in 2027. There was no real change to the revenue estimates, but the analysts do seem more bullish on earnings, given the solid gain to earnings per share expectations following these results.

Check out our latest analysis for Solaris Energy Infrastructure

There's been no major changes to the consensus price target of US$106, suggesting that the improved earnings per share outlook is not enough to have a long-term positive impact on the stock's valuation. The consensus price target is just an average of individual analyst targets, so - it could be handy to see how wide the range of underlying estimates is. Currently, the most bullish analyst values Solaris Energy Infrastructure at US$120 per share, while the most bearish prices it at US$72.00. Analysts definitely have varying views on the business, but the spread of estimates is not wide enough in our view to suggest that extreme outcomes could await Solaris Energy Infrastructure shareholders.

These estimates are interesting, but it can be useful to paint some more broad strokes when seeing how forecasts compare, both to the Solaris Energy Infrastructure's past performance and to peers in the same industry. It's clear from the latest estimates that Solaris Energy Infrastructure's rate of growth is expected to accelerate meaningfully, with the forecast 74% annualised revenue growth to the end of 2027 noticeably faster than its historical growth of 30% p.a. over the past five years. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in a similar industry are forecast to grow their revenue at 7.3% per year. It seems obvious that, while the growth outlook is brighter than the recent past, the analysts also expect Solaris Energy Infrastructure to grow faster than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing here is that the analysts upgraded their earnings per share estimates, suggesting that there has been a clear increase in optimism towards Solaris Energy Infrastructure following these results. Happily, there were no major changes to revenue forecasts, with the business still expected to grow faster than the wider industry. There was no real change to the consensus price target, suggesting that the intrinsic value of the business has not undergone any major changes with the latest estimates.

Keeping that in mind, we still think that the longer term trajectory of the business is much more important for investors to consider. At Simply Wall St, we have a full range of analyst estimates for Solaris Energy Infrastructure going out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here..

data.title: What Hindustan Zinc Holders Saw Early
data.description:
If Hindustan Zinc sat on your watchlist instead of in your demat account, the last twelve months may feel like a missed call. For Hindustan Zinc shareholders, the return over the past year was 21.8%, including dividends. That result arrived in a year when bullish and bearish analysts were split on whether an India infrastructure and EV upcycle would outweigh circular economy headwinds. If you rewind to November 2025, how confident could you really be that infrastructure demand would matter more than rising recycling pressures?

The move put Hindustan Zinc in the middle of this trade. Scan 33 best rare earth metal stocks for other companies exposed to it.

The Argument Hindustan Zinc Investors Faced Upfront

The shares cost ₹467 at the start of the period, and Hindustan Zinc holders had to decide which story about the future felt more reasonable.

The bullish narrative pinned a fair value of ₹564, a price level that flowed from assumptions rather than hard fact, built on the idea that revenue could grow 8.3% a year and margins could edge up from 31.3% to 32.0% by 2028.

The bearish view argued for a fair value of ₹335, tied to slower 4.7% annual revenue growth and concern that rising recycling and circular economy trends might cap demand for newly mined zinc.

What The Results Changed For Hindustan Zinc

The clearest marker was Hindustan Zinc’s Q2 2027 report. Revenue moved to ₹145,820 million and net income to ₹64,120 million, with net margin at 44.0% versus 32.0% a year earlier. That shift in profitability lined up more closely with the optimistic view that higher margins could matter more than recycling pressure, although long term demand risks stayed open.

The takeaway for you is simple. When an investment case leans on margin resilience, track net margin in the quarterly numbers and test whether it actually moves toward the story you were sold.

What Hindustan Zinc's Price Already Demands

Hindustan Zinc now trades at ₹568 after a 21.8% gain over the past year, while this Narrative’s Fair Value sits below the current price. The gap reflects concern that heavy expansion and diversification spend might not convert into equally strong long term returns.

For today’s level to hold up, you would need confidence that cost leadership and rising silver output can consistently fund growth projects and payouts without eroding cash generation.

"The numbers on volumes, margins, capital spending and payouts imply a share price that already bakes in successful execution on cost leadership, growth to roughly double metal capacity and higher value from silver and new minerals, with little room for disappointment."

One Narrative has put a figure on that disagreement. → See the Narrative with its lower Fair Value, assumptions and all

Looking One Step Beyond Hindustan Zinc

Hindustan Zinc links you to metals used in construction and electrification. One step away, another miner focuses on a different metal entirely.

This company targets unhedged exposure to gold and copper, not zinc. That focus keeps its fortunes closely aligned with movements in the gold price.

Management is pursuing higher grade ore, longer mine lives and deeper underground expansions. The shared goal is more metal from every tonne moved.

It is also committing significant cash to new projects while buying back shares and paying dividends. The unresolved question is how that balance might shift if conditions change.

Gold.com delivered a grave earnings miss, with both revenues (US$3.3b) and statutory earnings per share (US$0.05) falling badly short of analyst expectations. Earnings are an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance, look at what the analysts are forecasting for next year, and see if there's been a change in sentiment towards the company. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimates suggest is in store for next year.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Following the recent earnings report, the consensus from four analysts covering Gold.com is for revenues of US$21.5b in 2027. This implies a not inconsiderable 14% decline in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory per-share earnings are expected to be US$2.90, roughly flat on the last 12 months. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of US$21.5b and earnings per share (EPS) of US$2.74 in 2027. So the consensus seems to have become somewhat more optimistic on Gold.com's earnings potential following these results.

See our latest analysis for Gold.com

The consensus price target was unchanged at US$64.40, implying that the improved earnings outlook is not expected to have a long term impact on value creation for shareholders. It could also be instructive to look at the range of analyst estimates, to evaluate how different the outlier opinions are from the mean. The most optimistic Gold.com analyst has a price target of US$90.00 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at US$52.00. As you can see, analysts are not all in agreement on the stock's future, but the range of estimates is still reasonably narrow, which could suggest that the outcome is not totally unpredictable.

These estimates are interesting, but it can be useful to paint some more broad strokes when seeing how forecasts compare, both to the Gold.com's past performance and to peers in the same industry. These estimates imply that revenue is expected to slow, with a forecast annualised decline of 19% by the end of 2027. This indicates a significant reduction from annual growth of 24% over the last five years. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in the same industry are forecast to see their revenue grow 3.2% annually for the foreseeable future. It's pretty clear that Gold.com's revenues are expected to perform substantially worse than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The biggest takeaway for us is the consensus earnings per share upgrade, which suggests a clear improvement in sentiment around Gold.com's earnings potential next year. On the plus side, there were no major changes to revenue estimates; although forecasts imply they will perform worse than the wider industry. The consensus price target held steady at US$64.40, with the latest estimates not enough to have an impact on their price targets.

Following on from that line of thought, we think that the long-term prospects of the business are much more relevant than next year's earnings. We have forecasts for Gold.com going out to 2029, and you can see them free on our platform here.

data.title: Why Is Micron Technology (MU) At The Center Of A Global Chip Selloff?
data.description:
• Micron Technology (NasdaqGS:MU) is at the center of a sharp global selloff in semiconductor stocks tied to recent company setbacks.
  • The group has paused construction work at a plant site in Taiwan, raising questions about its future capacity plans in the region.
  • Investors are reacting to fresh concerns that post election US rules on AI infrastructure could tighten and affect Micron's business model.
  • Trading in chip makers across US tech indices and Korea's Kospi has turned volatile as markets reassess exposure linked to Micron's Taiwan plant pause and possible tighter US AI rules. Yet there is more to this story than today's shock. We have also flagged 4 other big wins for Micron Technology.

For a broader view on how AI hardware spending and regulation are shaping opportunities, it is worth examining 52 AI infrastructure stocks.

Micron Technology is a US based memory and storage producer that supplies chips used in data centers, AI servers and consumer electronics across Taiwan, Mainland China, other Asia Pacific markets, Japan, Europe and the US. Any disruption to its footprint can ripple across global supply chains.

Does the team leading Micron Technology have what it takes? See our full breakdown of the management team's track record and compensation.

Why has news around Micron Technology sparked such a broad semiconductor selloff?

Micron’s halted Taiwan plant construction, combined with fresh concerns about tighter US rules on AI data centers after the elections, has become a stress test for memory exposed stocks. Markets are quickly repricing how much AI driven demand can offset labor disputes, higher capital needs and possible regulatory friction for data center buildouts.

Does this change the Micron Technology Narrative investors have been leaning on?

The current shock leans straight into the Narrative’s key risk that heavy capex and tight DRAM or NAND conditions could be upset by execution problems in new fabs or labor constraints. At the same time, the news does not touch the core catalyst described there, long term customer agreements tied to AI memory that aim to turn tight supply into durable cash generation.

See how these catalysts shape Micron Technology's path to a $1,561 fair value.

How do leadership changes and board retirement plans feed into Micron’s direction?

Linnie M. Haynesworth plans to retire from the board after the January 2027 meeting, which will reduce Micron’s directors to eight and remove a chair with deep security and aerospace experience from its Security Committee. Investors will be watching how remaining committees absorb that portfolio and whether a successor reinforces areas like cybersecurity and AI infrastructure oversight.

What is the single development to watch next for Micron Technology after this selloff?

The clearest signal will be Micron’s next detailed update on its Taiwan buildout and US AI focused capacity plans, including whether the Taoyuan construction pause alters timelines, capex totals or its multi year supply commitments through 2030. A firm reaffirmation or reset of those concrete targets would either support or challenge the current Narrative built on tight supply and locked in demand.

data.title: AudioCodes Ltd. Just Beat Earnings Expectations: Here's What Analysts Think Will Happen Next
data.description:
There's been a major selloff in AudioCodes Ltd. (NASDAQ:AUDC) shares in the week since it released its quarterly report, with the stock down 30% to US$7.85. Revenues were US$64m, approximately in line with whatthe analyst expected, although statutory earnings per share (EPS) crushed expectations, coming in at US$0.15, an impressive 67% ahead of estimates. Following the result, the analyst has updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. Readers will be glad to know we've aggregated the latest statutory forecasts to see whether the analyst has changed their mind on AudioCodes after the latest results.

Taking into account the latest results, the most recent consensus for AudioCodes from lone analyst is for revenues of US$262.9m in 2027. If met, it would imply a satisfactory 4.4% increase on its revenue over the past 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to expand 11% to US$0.38. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analyst had been anticipated revenues of US$262.9m and earnings per share (EPS) of US$0.40 in 2027. So it looks like there's been a small decline in overall sentiment after the recent results - there's been no major change to revenue estimates, but the analyst did make a small dip in their earnings per share forecasts.

Althoughthe analyst has revised their earnings forecasts for next year, they've also lifted the consensus price target 29% to US$12.50, suggesting the revised estimates are not indicative of a weaker long-term future for the business.

One thing stands out from these estimates, which is that AudioCodes is forecast to grow faster in the future than it has in the past, with revenues expected to display 3.5% annualised growth until the end of 2027. If achieved, this would be a much better result than the 1.2% annual decline over the past five years. By contrast, our data suggests that other companies (with analyst coverage) in a similar industry are forecast to see their revenue grow 14% per year. So although AudioCodes' revenue growth is expected to improve, it is still expected to grow slower than the industry.

The Bottom Line

The biggest concern is that the analyst reduced their earnings per share estimates, suggesting business headwinds could lay ahead for AudioCodes. Fortunately, the analyst also reconfirmed their revenue estimates, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Although our data does suggest that AudioCodes' revenue is expected to perform worse than the wider industry. We note an upgrade to the price target, suggesting that the analyst believes the intrinsic value of the business is likely to improve over time.

Following on from that line of thought, we think that the long-term prospects of the business are much more relevant than next year's earnings. At least one analyst has provided forecasts out to 2027, which can be seen for free on our platform here.
